question: In which of the following states is the Chu-Faat dance performed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chu-Faat dance is a traditional dance form of the Lepcha community in Sikkim.
 
• This dance is performed in honor of Mount Khangchendzonga, the guardian deity of the Sikkim people.
 
• The dance involves the use of bamboo sticks and follows a rhythmic pattern.
 
• It is usually performed during festivals and special occasions in Sikkim.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikkim**

 
 
• Sikkim is a state in northeastern India. It borders Tibet in the north and northeast, Bhutan in the east, Nepal in the west, and West Bengal in the south.
 
• Sikkim is notable for its biodiversity, including alpine and subtropical climates, as well as being a host to Kangchenjunga, the highest peak in India and the third-highest on Earth.
 
• The state has a rich cultural heritage with diverse communities such as the Lepchas, Bhutias, and Nepalis.
 
• Sikkim is the least populous and second smallest among the Indian states.
 
 
 
• **Chu-Faat Dance**
 
 
• The dance is performed by the Lepcha community, who are considered to be the indigenous people of Sikkim.
 
• Chu-Faat is a ritualistic dance performed to honor and seek blessings from Mount Khangchendzonga.
 
• The dance is characterized by the use of bamboo sticks, which are symbolic of the mountains and the natural environment that the Lepchas revere.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional songs and music, which narrate the significance of the mountains and their role in the lives of the people.
